producer_report.summary: The reader brief and the producer brief now state the rule that every acceptance criterion must be checkable from the snapshot, the diff or the commands the verifier runs, never from the producer's report or change description. In briefs.rs a shared private const `CHECKABLE_CRITERIA_RULE` carries the sentence. The reader brief gets a `# Checkable criteria` section after the code survey guide and before `# What the verifier can run`. The producer brief gets a `## Make your evidence checkable` section just before `## criteria_check: copy the line`. It tells the producer to prefer a test in its change, add an evidence file only when a deliverable or criterion names it, and keep stating what it ran in its report. A criterion only the report could show is reported unmet, with evidence that begins `not checkable by the verifier`. Two new tests render each brief and assert on its text. In structure-pass.md section 5, every proof that lived only in the report now sits in the snapshot (committed tests and code) or in a command the verifier reruns (`--list`, the old-path Grep, `git diff`). Item 3 keeps its named exceptions. Item 5 says the proof is in the snapshot and no count is stored in a report. One CHANGELOG line was added. No prompt file, refusal logic or governance file changed, and briefs.rs has no removed lines.

mistakes: I first ran `cargo fmt --all` before the doc edits and then edited briefs.rs tests again after formatting. I formatted again afterwards and `cargo fmt --all --check` passes. I could not read the `cargo test --locked` output file to count its result lines.
learnings: The Bash tool rejects pipes, so `tail` after cargo does not work. Large cargo test output is saved to a file under ~/.claude that Read and Grep cannot open from the working directory.

READING_RULES is [&str; 8] and tests assert len 8, one check named per line, lines of at most 220 bytes and a rules section under 2600 bytes. A section with its own `# ` heading after CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE ends the rules section at `\n# `, so those tests read the same text as before.
The introspect.rs test `a_landing_touching_a_file_under_gh_selects_d87_and_d88` already exists, so 5.2 needed no new test.
desires: A way to read the saved output of a large cargo test run from inside the working directory, or a Bash form that works without pipes to see the final result lines.
